messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert — Dedicated pool `dedicated-42` p99 latency spike (>3s) detected. SLO breach. Auto-created incident channel: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2360007777 :rotating_light:
jessica: ack — paging oncall, grabbing runbook. Looking at dashboards now.
ops-bot: paging jessica, leo, tori. Pager sent to jessica (oncall).
jessica: I'm on it. p95 elevated but stable. p99 jumping to ~4s. Streaming stalls reported, queue depth for pool up ~5x.
leo: here — any customer reports? which regions affected?
maria: CS sees 3 tickets from EU tenants; customers report streaming stalls / long partial responses. One enterprise tenant reported complete timeouts for 30s.
jessica: mitigation plan: 1) manual scale +2 GPUs to pool dedicated-42; 2) enable temporary fallback routing to hosted-lite for non-enterprise traffic; 3) throttle low-priority batch routes. Executing step 1 now.
jessica: Running: `rictl pool scale --pool dedicated-42 --add-gpus 2`
ops-bot: Scale job queued (job id job-9982). Estimated attach/start ~45s.
tori: FYI logs show a lot of `warmup handshake timeout` entries and many warmup tasks stuck. Streaming stalls look correlated to handshake backlog rather than raw GPU saturation.
jessica: grabbing logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T09:02:11Z] warmup: handshake timeout after 10s, client_id=ab12
[2026-03-15T09:02:12Z] warmup: kv-cache miss, initiating weights load
[2026-03-15T09:02:13Z] streaming: chunk send stalled, wait for kernel init
```
leo: confirmed — autoscaler handshake queue length = 87, warmup tasks pending. The autoscaler control-plane is rate-limited; new nodes delayed. We should reduce incoming load to let warmups finish. Suggest immediate fallback routing for non-enterprise for 3m.
jessica: applying fallback: `routing set --policy fallback-hosted --duration 180 --filter 'tier!=enterprise'`
ops-bot: Fallback policy applied. All requests matching filter will be routed to hosted-lite variants.
maria: posting status page update now. Message: "Investigating elevated latency for dedicated deployments in EU. Mitigations in progress — manual scaling and routing changes. We will update within 15 minutes."
jessica: scale attach started — new nodes booting, warmup in progress. Warmup logs show parallelism low due to prior throttling.
tori: digging into root cause — control-plane autoscale handshakes are being requeued due to a burst earlier; we hit internal rate limits for pool operations. Also found a runaway warmup job from a prior test that pinned warmup workers. Opening ticket to adjust backoff/limits.
jessica: accelerating warmup: `rictl warmup --pool dedicated-42 --priority high --parallel 8` — kicking parallel warmup.
ops-bot: Warmup tasks started (taskset ts-776). Progress: 12/64 weights loaded on node-3.
leo: p95 improving, p99 dropping from 4.2s to ~1.9s after fallback + warmup. Tail latency still higher than baseline (~750ms p99). KV-cache cold miss rate still elevated.
jessica: also throttling the batch ingestion route: `quota set --route /batch --rate 50rps --duration 300` to reduce load on warmup.
maria: customer update sent to impacted tenants: "We've applied temporary routing and are scaling capacity; you may see improved performance in the next few minutes. We're continuing to monitor." Several customers acknowledged improvement.
tori: quick log excerpt — control-plane error causing handshake delay:
```
ERROR control-plane: rpc: rate limit exceeded while creating attach request
WARN warmup: worker starvation due to backoff
```
jessica: current metrics: queue depth returning to normal, p95 ~120ms, p99 ~1.1s. Streaming stalls largely resolved.
leo: leaving monitoring on this. I'll own follow-up and runbook updates. Actions to track: 1) increase autoscaler handshake throughput soft-limits, 2) prevent runaway warmup jobs, 3) add earlier auto-fallback when handshake backlog > threshold, 4) tune warmup parallelism.
jessica: handing oncall to leo for post-incident follow-up. oncall-handoff: @leo — I've documented mitigation steps in incident doc.
leo: got it. I'll monitor for 2 hours and draft PRs for the runbook changes.
ops-bot: Incident status: mitigation applied, monitoring.
maria: I'll follow up with customers this afternoon with a summary and RCA ETA.
jessica: quick root-cause summary for the thread: Dedicated pool saturation during burst + autoscaler control-plane rate-limiting caused attach/warmup delays; a leftover warmup job reduced parallelism and amplified handshake backlog, producing streaming stalls and p99 SLO breach. Short-term fixes: manual scale, fallback routing, throttle non-critical routes, accelerate warmup. Long-term: autoscaler backoff/limit changes, warmup safeguards, early fallback trigger.
leo: thanks all. I'll create the postmortem and assign owners for the remediation items.
incident-bot: Incident resolved: SLO recovered and customer impact mitigated. Closing通知.
